newsitem.title: Australia: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 6.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 6.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian football players less-than-fully committed to the AFL's State of Origin would be suspended if Victorian chairman of selectors Gerard Healy has his say. Healy has reiterated his call for tough penalties and increased match payments from the current A$3000, claiming clubs have had a tendency to encourage players to err on the side of caution when deciding whether to play Origin football. Page 20.

Caulfield Guiness winner Alfa has damaged a tendon which will see him sidelined until the spring. Jockey Darren Beadman and Alfa were scheduled to clash with Mouawad in the $A350,000 Cadbury Guiness (1600m) at Flemington on Saturday week in the build up to the AJC Derby (2400m) at Randwick on March 29. Page 20.

The Australian Baseball League board has determined that top-ladder finishers Perth Heat have lost their right to host the ABL championship playoff because of the clash of dates with the Sheffield Shield match at the WACA ground. However, the Perth front office is working to salvage at least the opening two games of the best-of-three series. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australia's rugby league honour in the World Sevens at the Sydney football Stadium this weekend against the US team, has fallen on the shoulders of Australian track team's Shane Naylor, Parramatta's Shane Whereat, Gold Coast's Shane Russell and Willie Goron a 17-year-old Riverview rugby scholarship winner. Page 48.

Australian national soccer league clubs were told yesterday they finally have the chance to compete internationally as the Asia-Pacific Football Cup is to proceed later this year. The tournament will provide the first serious attempt for Australian clubs for top-level international competition with up to eight countries from four continents potentially involved. Page 47.

Australian Rugby champion David Campese has been named alongside four other Wallabies in a 21-man world squad to play England's club champions at Twickenham on May 24. Campese retired from Test football last season after winning 101 caps for the Wallabies. Page 46.
THE AGE

The Australian Football League yesterday squashed a proposal from Victorian selection chairman Gerard Healy that reluctant state-of-origin players be suspended for one club match calling the move unworkable, saying it is impossible to determine whether players injuries were legitimate or not and to dispute medical reports. Page B8.

Australian swim star Michael Klim has returned to Melbourne for this week's sprint series and has already collected A$12,500 for his gold-medal wins at the Freestyle events during the recent short course world cup. He is waiting on Russian world record hoder Denis Pankratov to win two races this week so he can pick up another A$12,500 bonus prize money. Page B6.

Carlton president John Elliott has called on the State Government to help finance the proposed stadium at Docklands. Elliott claims unless the Kennett Government contributes financially to the A$350-million venue, ordinary football supporter will be unabe to afford a seat at games. Page B8.
THE HERALD SUN

Essendon coach Kevin Sheedy is attempting to start an historic overseas Australian Football League (AFL) match for premiership points, which if successful, would see a home-and-away international staged as early as next year. The match would place the Bobers against a Victorian-based opponent in a one-off home and away game at The Oval in London. Page 88.

Australian Football League's Geelong coach Gary Ayres, has said Gary Ablett's ability to play in the Ansett Cup series is in his own hands. Ablett has been battling to regain fitness and the Cats have allegedly run out of patience with their troubled chapion. Having given him as much time as possible, Ayres now says it is up to Ablett to decide how hungry he is to compete at the level he has in the last 13 years. Page 85.

Australian Soccer last night confirmed the Socceroos' match against the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia in Skopje on March 12 and a second game against Hungary in Budapest on April 2. Coach Terry Venables decided to pull out of negotiations with Croatia before flying to England to start preparations. Page 82.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australia's Mark Woodforde may be selected to play with Patrick Rafter in tomorrow's Davis Cup tennis ties against France at White City. Captain John Newcombe said yesterday the team selection has been one of the toughest in the two years since he and Rohe had taken over from Neale Fraser. Page 80.

A Court heard yesterday that Penrith star Steve Carter had been warned by NSW State of Origin coach Phil Gould he would never play representative football again if he joined Super League. In an attempt to get the Penrith player to sign loyalty agreements with the ARL, Gould warned Carter that Super League's promised payout could not be honoured because they were only on a A$2 shelf company. Page 78.

Sydney golfer Peter Lonard flew from Perth on Tuesday to the Gold Coast via Kalgoorlie, Adelaide and Sydney in a 15-hour trip for one putting lesson with coach Gary Edwin at Hope Island. Lonard believes the 6000km trip was necessary for some finetuning for the $A300,000 Ford Open at Kooyonga which starts today. Page 79.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
